front.title: Consented and Attributable Agent Authority for Operational-Technology Control Actions

abstract.t: This memo specifies a binding profile by which a control action issued to an operational-technology (OT) or industrial control system on the authority of a software agent is refused unless it carries a verifiable statement of who the agent is, which human principal it acts for, whether that principal authorised this specific action on this specific asset, whether a named human signed off on the action where its risk class requires it, and an append-only record sufficient to attribute the action afterward. The profile does not invent new cryptography or a new identity mechanism. It composes primitives specified elsewhere, DNSSEC-rooted agent discovery, a scoped and revocable authorisation grant, a named-human authorization receipt bound into the record as human-authorization evidence, and an append-only transparency record, into a single structure, the Command Authority Envelope, that an enforcement point evaluates and, on any missing or invalid binding, refuses. The profile is availability- first and fails closed on authority, never on safety: it MUST NOT be placed in the trip path of a safety function. The memo maps the profile onto the identification, use-control, and audit requirements that the IEC 62443 and NERC CIP frameworks state but do not give a wire mechanism for. A neighbouring proposal gates safety-critical commands on an agent's trust level; this profile takes the opposite position, and states why. The methods by which a principal's identity is inferred are out of scope by construction.
